chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad who said:
I prayed behind al-Rida (peace be upon him) in al-Masjid al-Haram the night prayer, and when he finished, he made the place of the sitting (qa'dah) a prostration.

key_terms.اَلرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the tenth Imam, Ali ibn Musa)
key_terms.اَلضَّجْعَةُ: The sitting position (referring to the final sitting or a specific sitting in prayer)
key_terms.صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ: The night prayer (Tahajjud or specific night worship)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida conclude the night prayer in terms of prostration and sitting?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam al-Rida’s (AS) specific practice in the night prayer (Salat al-Layl) within the Grand Mosque, where he substituted the final sitting position (qa'dah) with an additional prostration (sajdah). This unique ritual detail reflects the distinct jurisprudential traditions (fiqh) of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the structure and devotion of voluntary night prayers, emphasizing the spiritual depth and physical humility associated with concluding such worship.
